title: Electronic digital computers and operating systems

paras: Technology, infrastructure, network architecture, institutional ownership and business economics.
Vacuum-tube electronic digital machines, stored-program memory, transistors, magnetic-core memory, magnetic tape, integrated circuits, batch monitors and time-sharing.

blocks.h2: Who developed, funded, owned and operated the systems?
paras: Universities, government laboratories, IBM, DEC, Bell Labs, semiconductor firms and defense research sponsors. These participants had different roles: research sponsorship, equipment supply, network operation, regulation, standardization and service consumption should not be conflated.
Central computer with peripherals and terminals; jobs scheduled and protected by emerging operating-system mechanisms.
Mainframe purchase or leasing, maintenance, centralized computing services, time-sharing fees.

Digital refers to discrete representation; electronic refers to implementation. The transition was from electromechanical and isolated computing to faster electronic digital, interactive and shared systems.
A payroll batch could be submitted on cards, executed by a central machine and printed later. Time-sharing subsequently let multiple terminals interact with one computer through scheduled CPU access.
Expensive computing encouraged centralized ownership; resource scheduling and access controls became economically and administratively important.
